ordered_diagnoses: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Caruncle

facts.raw_span: a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
The specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm and had a 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Revealed a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Showed positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor
Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells
Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A

concepts.why: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, pedunculated mass with positive reactivity to melanocytic markers supports this diagnosis.
The absence of pigmentation and the presence of anaplastic cells with mitotic activity support this diagnosis.
The presence of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity supports this diagnosis, although it is less likely given the positive reactivity to melanocytic markers.

The absence of evidence of PAM supports this diagnosis, although it is less likely given the presence of a rapidly growing mass.

The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells, indicating a high proliferative index, and sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative, which are consistent with malignant melanoma.

rationales.F01: Rapid growth of the lesion suggests malignancy.
rationales.F02: Amelanotic and pedunculated mass with ulcerated surface is characteristic of malignant melanoma.
rationales.F05: Anaplastic cells with mitotic activity indicate high-grade malignancy.
rationales.F06: Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers confirms melanoma.
rationales.F11: Mitotically active tumor with anaplastic epithelioid cells suggests aggressive malignancy.
